# Find a capability from the need

Start from what the picture needs. Each need lists every construction that serves it, the names to use (operation kinds for `applyOperations`, Action ids, `listCapabilities` sections and keys of its answer with no arguments, tools, plugin commands), what a person can change afterwards in Studio, and what each construction gives up. How the parts work together is the `model` section. For a kind's exact input, conditions and examples that stage, call `listCapabilities` with `kinds` (for example {"kinds": ["addMorph"]}); `operations` lists every kind with its fields.

## Shots and the film

**A new shot, or the next beat of the film**
- A new Scene: its own duration, background, objects, Actions and camera, played after the others → `addScene`, `duplicateScene`, `updateSceneDuration`, `updateSceneName`, `reorderScene`, `removeScene`
  Studio: the Scene strip adds, duplicates, reorders and deletes Scenes; dragging the end of the Scene's band on the timeline sets its length. Gives up: object and Action ids are Scene-local and nothing carries across a cut by itself.
- Stay in one Scene and change the composition with Actions and the camera → sections `actions`, `camera`
  Gives up: one longer timeline; continuity is free, but a person retimes the beats inside one Scene.

**A join between two shots**
- A transition at the boundary: fade, crossfade, iris, slide, zoom, linear or clock wipe, barn door, match cut, or your own SkSL with `shaderTransition` → `setTransition`, `removeTransition` · `listCapabilities` with no arguments: key `transitionKinds`
  Studio: the button between two Scenes on the strip opens the transition: kind, duration, behavior, curve and direction. Gives up: `hold` freezes the outgoing Scene's last frame while the next one plays, so the film keeps its length; `overlap` plays both and shortens the film. One transition per boundary.
- One element carried across the cut: a `sharedElement` transition naming an object id present in both Scenes → `setTransition`
  Gives up: the object needs the same id in both Scenes, may not be a mask member in either, and neither Scene may carry Scene post effects.
- No transition: Scenes cut
  Gives up: nothing to tune; continuity has to come from matched compositions.

**The film's size, frame rate and name**
- Set the project format and name → `setProjectFormat`, `updateProjectMeta` · tool `createProject`
  Studio: format presets and the project name.

**The backdrop behind everything in a Scene**
- A solid, gradient or transparent Scene background → `updateSceneBackground`, `setSceneBackgroundFill`
  Studio: the Scene inspector's background.
- A living background: a Shader on the `sceneBackground` scope → `addShader` · sections `visualCatalog`, `shaderAuthoring`
  Gives up: Studio keys a Shader's Properties and has no SkSL editor.

## Things on screen

**Words on screen**
- A Text object; size it with `textSizing` (auto width for titles and labels, auto height for paragraphs, fixed for a set box) → `addObject` · sections `fontFaces`, `examples` · `listCapabilities` with no arguments: keys `text`, `fonts`
  Studio: type on the canvas; font, size, weight, alignment and spacing in the Design panel. Gives up: a family must be one the server lists in `fonts`, and the stage binds the faces a Text uses itself; a character no font covers paints as a box, and `renderFrame` names it.

**A card, a pill, a circle, a polygon or a star**
- A shape object: rectangle, ellipse, polygon or star → `addObject` · `listCapabilities` with no arguments: keys `shape`, `authoringGuide`
  Studio: drawn with the shape tool; corner radius, fill and stroke in the Design panel; vector editing turns a primitive into custom geometry. Gives up: a shape's custom geometry is made in Studio; for a custom outline, draw a network Path. A shape's stroke sits inside its box; shapes cannot be drawn on or guide a Follow Path (use a network Path). In a project made before the empty-fill default, a shape with no fill paints black, so a stroke-only shape there takes a fully transparent fill (the overview's fill guide says how to tell).

**A freeform line or outline**
- A network Path: straight segments with `addPath`, curves and several contours with `addVectorNetwork`, a later redraw with `replaceVectorNetwork` → `addPath`, `addVectorNetwork`, `replaceVectorNetwork` · sections `path`, `canvasCreation` · tool `inspectPathRegions`
  Studio: the pen and pencil tools and vector editing work on the same network. Gives up: every stroke trail needs a name; raw SVG path data is never authored. Resizing a network Path with `updateObjectBase` scales its geometry and keeps its stroke width.

**A photo, a screenshot or a clip**
- Upload the file, add it as an asset, then an image or video object fitted with `objectFit` → `addAsset`, `addObject` · `listCapabilities` with no arguments: key `authoringGuide` · tool `createMediaUpload`
  Studio: Fit in the image's or video's inspector. Gives up: a video's media time is its Scene's time plus its in point (`inMs`), so one that appears mid-Scene is already that far in, and past its out point it holds the last frame; no speed change, reverse or loop. `renderFrame` paints a library video as its first frame.

**Things that belong together: a group that moves, fades or clips as one**
- A Frame holding the children; each child names it with `parentId` and is placed from the Frame's top-left → `addObject`, `setObjectParent` · `listCapabilities` with no arguments: key `authoringGuide`
  Studio: the Layers panel nests and reorders; the Frame inspector holds fill, Clip contents and auto layout. Gives up: a Frame with no fill and no stroke paints nothing itself; a Frame cannot be a mask target.

**A row or column that spaces and reflows its items**
- Auto layout on a Frame: direction, gap, padding, alignment, wrap; each child hugs, fills or stays fixed → `setAutoLayout`, `setLayoutSizing`, `updateObjectBase` · section `autoLayout`
  Studio: the Auto layout section of the Frame inspector, and each child's layout sizing. Gives up: a flow Frame places its flow children itself, from their design boxes: a child's Scale or Rotation does not make room. There is no grid mode, and changes between hug, fixed and fill are hard cuts.
- Absolute children placed by hand in a plain Frame → `updateObjectBase`
  Gives up: nothing reflows when an item changes size.

**Front and back**
- Layer order among siblings: a higher `layer` paints in front → `setObjectLayer`
  Studio: drag rows in the Layers panel. Gives up: order is among siblings of one parent; under a projective camera siblings also sort by depth.

**Change how an existing object looks or where it sits**
- Edit its design state: position, size, opacity, scale, rotation and 3D in the base; fill, stroke, blur and type in the style; its content → `updateObjectBase`, `updateObjectStyle`, `setObjectPrimaryFill`, `updateObjectContent`, `renameObject`, `removeObject` · section `objectProperties`
  Studio: the Design panel and the canvas handles. Gives up: a style key set on a kind it does not apply to paints nothing and the stage warns; `objectProperties` lists which kinds each key applies to. Change fills with `setObjectPrimaryFill`, not the style.

## Movement

**Slide, drift, rise, enter from a side**
- A Move Action: it adds to the design position (a key's value less its track's `baseValue`) → `materializeActionFacets` · Action `move` · sections `actions`, `examples`
  Studio: keys on the timeline, the motion path on the canvas, key values in the inspector. Gives up: travel between keys is a straight line; easing changes the speed, not the path.

**Travel along a curve: an arc, an orbit, a cursor gliding to a target**
- Follow Path along a guide Path, which may have no stroke → `addFollowPath`, `updateFollowPathActionSettings` · Action `followPath` · section `path`
  Studio: guide, trail, direction, orient to path, progress from and to, offsets and timing. Gives up: a Follow holds after it ends, so it owns the follower's x and y (and rotation when oriented) from its start until the follower's lifetime ends, its guide (a network Path in the same Scene) must live that long, and the follower takes no second Follow Path in that lifetime: put other motion on a parent Frame, and change paths by handing over to another object. 3D on either chain below their shared parent, a warp or a Repeater anywhere on either chain, or a zero scale is refused.
- Several Move keys → Action `move`
  Gives up: straight chords between keys: a polygon, not a curve.
- Rotate a parent Frame about a pivot (`originX`, `originY`) with the object as its child → Action `rotation`
  Gives up: only circular arcs; the child turns with the Frame unless it counter-rotates.

**Grow, shrink, pop, push in on a group**
- A Scale Action: keys multiply the design scale → `materializeActionFacets` · Action `scale`
  Gives up: strokes, corners and text scale too.
- A Resize Action: the box grows and keeps stroke weight and corner radius → Action `resize`
  Gives up: shapes, paths, images and Frames only (no text or video).
- The `scale-pop` preset expands into ordinary Actions → `applyPreset` · section `presets`

**Spin, tilt, flip, turn a card in 3D**
- Rotation for the flat turn; 3D Rotate for X and Y with its own perspective; Depth Z toward or away from the viewer → `materializeActionFacets`, `update3dRotateActionConstants` · Actions `rotation`, `3dRotate`, `depthZ`
  Studio: the orientation trackball and the transform fields; the 3D Rotate perspective and faces in its inspector. Gives up: a new 3D Rotate starts its perspective at the object's own (1000 when it has none) and replaces it while it runs or holds; Depth Z shows only under perspective or a projective camera.

**Fade in, fade out, dim**
- An Opacity Action; on a Frame it fades the Frame and its children as one image → `materializeActionFacets` · Action `opacity` · section `examples`
- Background Opacity fades only a Frame's own fill and stroke → Action `backgroundOpacity`

**Box to pill to circle; panels that open**
- Corner Radius and Resize Actions → Actions `cornerRadius`, `resize`
  Gives up: Corner Radius applies to shapes, images, videos and Frames; not to paths or text.
- A Morph for a change of silhouette rather than of box → `addMorph` · Action `morph` · section `geometryMorph`

**Items in a row make room, swap places or change direction smoothly**
- A layout transition on the flow Frame: an expression block with a `layout.state` primitive moves the children from the current arrangement to a new direction, alignment, order or set of present children over its window, then holds → `addMotionBlock` · section `autoLayout`
  Studio: the block's range, and its direction, justify, align and wrap when they are bound to controls. Gives up: two transitions on one Frame may not overlap; `layoutSizing` and `reverseZIndex` still cut; a child that leaves keeps its slot while the others close the gap, and fading it is its own Action.
- Absolute children moved by hand → Action `move`
  Gives up: nothing reflows; each position is keyed by hand.

**Spacing that breathes: a gap or padding that opens and closes**
- A Layout Spacing Action on a flow Frame; its children reflow every frame → Action `layoutSpacing` · section `autoLayout`
  Gives up: flow Frames only; padding stays at 0 or above while a gap may go negative.

**Recolour a fill or a stroke**
- Color (fill) and Stroke (colour and width) Actions → Actions `color`, `stroke` · `listCapabilities` with no arguments: key `colorInterpolation`
  Gives up: colour keys travel in HSLA, so far hues sweep around the wheel and saturated-to-dark passes through muddy tones; springs are refused on colour. Gradient stop positions and angle do not animate.
- Cross-fade two layers with Opacity → Action `opacity`
  Gives up: two objects to keep aligned.

**Type that tracks out, opens up or gets heavier**
- Letter Spacing, Line Height and Font Weight Actions on a whole Text → Actions `letterSpacing`, `lineHeight`, `fontWeight`
  Gives up: whole object only. Weight moves continuously on a family with `variable` in `fontFaces` and steps between faces on others, which the stage warns about.

**A shadow that lifts or moves**
- A Shadow Action, created or adopted from a drop shadow with `materializeShadowFacet`; `updateShadowStaticFacet` changes its static values and `makeShadowActionStatic` makes it still again → `materializeShadowFacet`, `updateShadowStaticFacet`, `makeShadowActionStatic` · Action `shadow` · tool `getSceneAuthoringContext`
  Gives up: not on Frames; each of these operations needs the shadow fingerprint `getSceneAuthoringContext` serves.
- A drop shadow Effect, retuned later → `addObjectEffect`, `updateShaderValues` · `listCapabilities` with no arguments: key `effects`

**A value computed from a formula: a sway, a pulse, per-copy maths, a channel no Action drives**
- An expression block: values from time ramps, springs, controls and arithmetic (add, subtract, multiply, divide, sin, cos, clamp, lerp), on channels such as skew, origin, brightness, hue, `clip.progress` and `mask.inset` → `addMotionBlock`, `updateMotionBlockControls`, `updateMotionBlockRange`, `addPrimitive`, `removePrimitive`, `updatePrimitive` · section `objectProperties` · `listCapabilities` with no arguments: keys `primitiveKinds`, `interpolateEasing`, `controlValueShapes`
  Studio: its controls and its range; Studio lists what the program writes but changes it only through the controls. Gives up: it must expose at least one number or colour control its program reads; there is no noise, random, wiggle or loop function.

## Timing and feel

**Ease in, ease out, a custom curve, a held step**
- Each key's `outgoingTiming`: a named easing, a cubic bezier, a spring, a `hold`, or a shared timing style → `updateMotionSegmentTiming`, `setProjectDefaultSegmentTiming` · `listCapabilities` with no arguments: key `easings` · tool `getSceneAuthoringContext`
  Studio: the timing popup edits each segment: named easings, a draggable bezier, spring bounciness and speed, Hold.

**A springy settle, an overshoot**
- A spring segment → `listCapabilities` with no arguments: key `controlValueShapes`
  Gives up: a spring runs in seconds from its left key, so the segment's length does not set its speed, and an unsettled spring jumps to the next key; not on colour.
- Keys that overshoot and come back, or a back or elastic easing → `listCapabilities` with no arguments: key `easings`
  Gives up: the overshoot is drawn by hand, key by key.

**One curve shared by many Actions, changed in one place**
- A project timing style that segments reference live → `createTimingStyle`, `setTimingStyleValue`, `renameTimingStyle`, `deleteTimingStyle` · section `timingStyles`
  Studio: the timing popup applies, detaches, creates, renames, edits and deletes styles. Gives up: a style is an easing or a spring for good; the family cannot change later.

**B starts when A ends**
- Sequencing: an Action follows another's end plus a delay, live → `updateMotionBlockSequencing`
  Studio: dragging a chained Action changes its delay and keeps it attached; an expression block's Start switches between absolute and after another block. Gives up: a block in a stagger group cannot also be sequenced.

**A cast of different items arriving in order**
- One Action per member joined in a stagger group: delay and order (forward, reverse, center-out) in one place → `addStaggerGroup`, `updateStaggerGroup`, `removeStaggerGroup`
  Studio: Stagger Actions groups a multi-selection; delay and order are edited in one place. Gives up: members must not carry sequencing.
- Identical copies with a Copies stagger (see Repeater) → `addRepeater`, `updateMotionBlockRepeaterStagger` · section `repeater`

**Several Actions of one object moved and named as one unit**
- A motion block group: editing metadata over existing Actions of one object, with its own retime → `addMotionBlockGroup`, `updateMotionBlockGroup`, `removeMotionBlockGroup`, `reorderMotionBlockGroup`, `retimeMotionBlockGroup`
  Gives up: it changes nothing on screen by itself; two members at least.

## Appearing and leaving

**Appear at a moment, leave at a moment**
- Give the first entrance Action the stage `in` and the exit the stage `out`: the object exists from the entrance's start to the exit's end → `materializeActionFacets`, `updateMotionBlockStage` · section `actions`
  Studio: the object's lifetime bar on the timeline follows its In and Out Actions.
- A lifetime `range` for an object with no entrance or exit animation → `setObjectRange`
  Studio: Lifetime start and end in the inspector, or the whole Scene. Gives up: an In or Out Action's stage overrides the matching end. Hiding with base opacity 0 is not a lifetime.

**Stay put after moving, or snap back**
- An Action's After: `hold` keeps its last value, `release` returns to the design value → `setMotionWritePersistence` · `listCapabilities` with no arguments: key `persistence`
  Studio: After in the Action's inspector.

**Swap a word, show or hide in one frame, step a counter**
- Event Actions at one frame: Hide, Show, Change Text → `addEventAction` · Actions `hide`, `show`, `changeText`
  Studio: events retime on the timeline; Change Text edits its text. Gives up: a counter is one event per step.
- Two objects with lifetimes, or a cross-fade → `setObjectRange` · Action `opacity`

## Type in motion

**Letters or words arriving one by one**
- One Action on the text's word or letter segments with a `segmentSchedule`: stagger, direction, humanize and per-segment windows → `materializeActionFacets`, `updateMotionSegmentSchedule` · section `actions` · `listCapabilities` with no arguments: key `text`
  Studio: the schedule (distribution, delay, direction, humanize, template duration, After) and each segment's window on the timeline. Gives up: segments animate position, opacity, scale, rotation, blur and fill only; there is no line unit, so use one Text per line. Never one Action per letter.
- A preset that expands into the same scheduled Actions: `typewriter`, `cascade-in`, `cascade-out`, `soft-word-build`, `accent-color` → `applyPreset` · section `presets`
  Gives up: the text's segment mode must match the preset's unit.

**Typing with a blinking caret**
- A caret on a letter-schedule Action; it follows the typing frontier from the same schedule → `addTextCaret`
  Gives up: removing the Action removes the caret; the caret shows only while its text does.

**A number that counts up**
- The `odometer` preset: rolling digit columns that count from 0 to the number the text shows → `applyPreset` · section `presets`
  Gives up: the text must be digits, optionally grouped by , . ' or a space; units such as % and + go in a separate Text.
- Change Text events, one per step → `addEventAction` · Action `changeText`
- Not in the medium: a numeric text tween.

**New copy, a styled word, bigger type, without losing the motion**
- Replace the text or a range of it; style a range → `replaceTextSnapshot`, `replaceTextRange`, `setTextRangeStyle` · tool `getSceneAuthoringContext`
  Gives up: each needs the text's snapshot fingerprint from `getSceneAuthoringContext`; an edit that would strand segment motion is refused and names it.
- Scale all of a Text's typography by one factor → `scaleTextTypography` · tool `getSceneAuthoringContext`
  Gives up: it needs the Text's `expectedTextTimelineFingerprint` and `expectedObjectTypographyFingerprint`, which `getSceneAuthoringContext` serves for each Text; read them again after any accept.

## Lines and strokes

**An ink stroke that draws on; a line that draws itself**
- A Draw Action on a network Path's named trails, over any frame range → `addDrawErase`, `updateDrawEraseActionSettings` · Action `draw` · section `path`
  Studio: route (trails and their order), direction, range, start point and duration. Gives up: the Path needs a visible stroke; shapes and connectors cannot be drawn on.
- `drawOn` on a new `addPath` → `addPath`
  Gives up: it always starts at frame 0 with a short ramp; use a Draw for a timed one.
- A preset that adds a drawn stroke to an object: `underline-draw`, `doodle-stroke`, `arc-sweep`, `checkbox-draw` → `applyPreset` · section `presets`
  Gives up: the preset decides the stroke's shape.

**A stroke that leaves, a comet, a scanning line**
- An Erase Action; a Draw plus an overlapping Erase in the reverse direction on the same trails make a travelling stroke (the Draw moves the head, the Erase the tail) → `addDrawErase` · Actions `erase`, `draw`

**A brush, marker, chalk or hand-drawn stroke**
- A brush from the library: six stretch, six scatter and four dry brushes → `applyPathBrushPreset` · section `path` · tool `listBrushLibrary`
  Studio: brush parameters; a seed can be re-rolled. Gives up: single-contour, single-trail network Paths.
- A stroke treatment: dynamic wobble, or a stretch or scatter brush from your own vector source → `setPathStrokeTreatment` · section `path`
  Gives up: dashes work only on a basic uniform stroke; dry brushes come only from the library.

**A stroke that tapers or swells**
- A width profile: a preset taper or your own points along the stroke → `setPathStrokeWidthProfile` · section `path`

**A line that connects two things and follows them**
- A connector between two objects: straight, curved or elbow, with an optional arrowhead → `addConnector`
  Studio: routing, arrowhead, curvature and padding; not its endpoints. Gives up: its draw-on starts at frame 0; it cannot be drawn with a Draw Action or guide a Follow.
- A network Path drawn between them → `addVectorNetwork`
  Gives up: it does not follow the objects when they move.

## Shapes into shapes

**Two shapes become one; cut one shape out of another**
- The Region Builder inside one network Path: merge the selected regions into one, or subtract them → `mergePathRegions`, `subtractPathRegions` · section `path` · tools `planPathRegionBuilder`, `mergePathRegions`, `subtractPathRegions`
  Studio: Merge and Subtract in vector edit mode. Gives up: both outlines must be contours of one network Path; the change is to geometry, not animated.
- Merge gives the exact joined outline, closed, and a Morph can animate into it: Merge a copy that holds both outlines, then Morph the separate shapes into that Path → `mergePathRegions`, `addMorph` · Action `morph`
- Morph one outline into the combined silhouette over time → `addMorph` · Action `morph`
- An inverted mask for a cut-out look → `addMaskBinding`
  Gives up: the geometry stays whole; only what shows changes.

**Colour one enclosed area of a line drawing**
- Paint a region of a network Path → `paintPathRegion` · section `path` · tools `inspectPathRegions`, `paintPathRegion`
  Studio: region paint (Shift+B) in vector edit mode.

**Lift a region out as its own shape**
- Materialize the selected regions as a new Path; the source stays as it was → `materializePathRegionSelection` · section `path` · tools `planPathRegionMaterialization`, `materializePathRegionSelection`

**A logo turns into an arrow; one silhouette becomes another**
- A Morph from a shape or network Path into another object's outline, a primitive or a network → `addMorph`, `setMorphTarget`, `setMorphCorrespondence` · Action `morph` · section `geometryMorph`
  Studio: the target, the fit, how shapes are matched, the pairs, and timing. Gives up: outlines are interpolated point to point, not blended like metaballs; open and closed contours do not pair; a Path with region paints cannot host. The stage answer reports how the outlines were paired.
- Cross-fade two objects → Action `opacity`
  Gives up: no in-between shapes.

## Reveal and cover

**A layer that appears only inside another shape, or inside letters**
- A mask: one source supplies coverage to one sibling target; `vector` uses the source's outline (shape, path or text), `alpha` its painted alpha (also image or video); `inverted` flips it → `addMaskBinding`, `updateMaskBinding`, `removeMaskBinding`
  Studio: Use as Mask; mode and Invert in the inspector; the Layers panel marks the pair. Gives up: the source paints nothing itself; an object belongs to at most one mask, so one source cannot cover two targets; the target is a leaf (not a Frame) with the same parent; refused under a projective camera or a 3D pose, under a Frame with an Effect, and on a Repeater, its Original included. Animate the source and target, never the binding.
- A Frame that clips its children to its rounded box → `updateObjectStyle` · `listCapabilities` with no arguments: key `containerClip`
  Studio: Clip contents in the Frame inspector. Gives up: the window is a rounded rectangle, but it clips whole groups and works in 3D.

**A wipe or a reveal that travels**
- Animate the mask source (Move, Scale, Resize, Morph) or the clipping Frame (Resize, Corner Radius) → Actions `move`, `scale`, `resize`, `cornerRadius`
- The expression channels `clip.progress` and `mask.inset` → `addMotionBlock` · section `objectProperties`
- A scrolling feed or list inside a window: Content Offset on a clipping Frame → Action `contentOffset`
- Not in the medium: luma mattes; a mask on a Frame group (a Frame cannot be a target).

## Many things at once

**A row, a grid or a field of identical dots, bars or tiles**
- A Repeater: one Original plus generated Copies in a line or grid, with deterministic variation across copies; motion addresses the Original, all Copies (with a stagger) or the whole Field → `addRepeater`, `setObjectRepeater`, `updateMotionBlockRepeaterStagger` · section `repeater`
  Studio: layout, count, spacing, offsets, copies' fill and opacity, variation ranges, Field Mesh; Copies and Field Actions authored by an agent can be retimed, re-keyed, re-staggered and deleted, not restructured. Gives up: every copy shows the template's content (no per-copy text); no radial or on-path layout; at most 200 copies.
- Separate objects with a stagger group → `addStaggerGroup`
  Gives up: many objects to keep consistent, but each can differ.

## Light, colour and texture

**Glow, drop shadow, a colour grade, an outline, film grain**
- An Effect on the object; a second of the same kind is appended under its own id → `addObjectEffect`, `appendObjectEffect`, `updateShaderValues`, `keyShaderProperty` · section `designPropertyAnimation` · `listCapabilities` with no arguments: key `effects`
  Studio: the Effects section lists each Effect, edits its Properties and keys them. Gives up: a shadow is keyed through its Shadow Action (`materializeShadowFacet`), not `keyShaderProperty`. On a Frame an Effect filters the whole subtree as one image; a Shader Effect on a Frame is dropped when a descendant is 3D, warped or repeated.

**A living colour field, a texture, glass, a whole-frame grade**
- A ready-made look from the library on one of five scopes: an object's fill (`objectFill`), the Scene background (`sceneBackground`), an Effect on an object (`objectEffect`), what shows behind an object (`objectBackdrop`), or the whole composited Scene (`scenePostEffect`) → `addShader`, `updateShaderValues`, `keyShaderProperty` · section `visualCatalog`
  Studio: slides and keys the look's Properties and retunes its phase ramp. Gives up: only the values the entry exposes as Properties can change.
- A look of your own on any of those scopes. Write the SkSL yourself and decide which of its values a person can retune and keyframe in Studio: each of those is a Property, declared with its control and read in the source as its uniform. Every other value is a constant in the source, which Studio cannot change: it has no SkSL editor. Time is a Property too: there is no time uniform, so declare a number Property and name it in `shader.phase`, and the server drives it with a linear ramp whose speed and offset a person can retune. Check each version with `compileShader` before `addShader`; retune a placed Shader's values with `updateShaderValues`, and key them over time with `keyShaderProperty`. → `addShader`, `updateShaderValues`, `keyShaderProperty` · section `shaderAuthoring` · tool `compileShader`
  Studio: a person retunes and keyframes the Properties you exposed; it has no SkSL editor. Gives up: a constant changes only with a new version of the SkSL, and a placed Shader keeps the version it has; a placement paints its Property defaults on frames no block writes.

**A gradient fill**
- A linear, radial or conic gradient as the object's fill → `setObjectPrimaryFill`, `addObject`
  Gives up: stop positions and angle do not animate; move a larger gradient object inside a clipping Frame or use a Shader for a moving gradient.
- Not in the medium: gradient strokes; outline a filled shape instead.

**Add, screen or multiply light between layers**
- Build light with a Shader or with opacity layering → `addShader` · Action `opacity`
- Not in the medium: layer blend modes.

## Blur and speed

**Speed that smears: motion blur**
- Motion blur on the object, `style.motionBlur`: a shutter in project frames (0.5 is a 180° shutter), adaptive or fixed samples; the Motion Blur Action keys the shutter → `updateObjectStyle`, `setMotionBlurQuality` · Action `motionBlur`
  Studio: the Motion Blur card: on or off, the shutter as an angle, adaptive or fixed sampling; the project's quality in Export. Gives up: it blurs transform motion only and never samples across a Scene edge or a camera cut; adaptive sampling reads the object's box sweep, so letters moving inside a still Text get the still count.
- Layer Blur keyed by hand → Action `layerBlur`
  Gives up: not motion blur: it blurs in every direction, whatever the motion.
- Not in the medium: directional blur.

**Focus pulls, a soft arrival, frosted glass**
- Layer Blur on an object (on a Frame, the Frame and everything in it as one image) → Action `layerBlur`
  Gives up: a blur radius r is a Gaussian with σ = r/2 in the object's own units, so CSS blur(v) is radius 2v.
- Background Blur behind a shape or path with a partly transparent fill → Action `backgroundBlur`
- Camera focus: depth of field on a projective camera → Action `cameraFocus` · section `camera`
  Gives up: blurs only with `maxBlurPx` and a focus falloff above 0.

## Camera and depth

**Push in, pan, frame a subject, cut between framings**
- A camera shot that frames an object, a rect, a point or a pose, baked into an ordinary Camera Frame Action → `addCameraShot` · Action `cameraFrame` · section `camera`
  Studio: the Camera lane on the timeline: shots as rows with keys; + adds a shot at the playhead. Gives up: nothing stays bound to the object: if it moves later, re-frame. Where shots overlap, the later in the Scene's order wins.
- Camera Actions keyed by hand → `materializeActionFacets` · Actions `cameraFrame`, `cameraRoll`, `cameraDolly`, `cameraTilt`, `cameraLens`, `cameraFocus` · section `camera`
- Move a world Frame that holds the Scene → Actions `move`, `scale`
  Gives up: no depth, focus or lens; everything else in the Scene must live inside that Frame.

**Parallax and real depth**
- A projective camera (a dolly, a tilt or a lens) over layers at different depths → `setSceneCamera`, `updateSceneCamera` · Actions `cameraDolly`, `cameraTilt`, `cameraLens`, `depthZ` · section `camera` · `listCapabilities` with no arguments: key `authoringGuide`
  Studio: the Scene camera section: position, zoom, roll, perspective, tilt, depth, focus. Gives up: layers sort as whole layers, not per pixel; masks are refused under a projective camera; read on-screen boxes with `previewRange`.
- The `parallax-pan` or `depth-push-in` recipe → `applyRecipe` · section `recipes`

**A camera shake or a small accent on top of the framing**
- A camera recipe: `camera-shake`, `camera-push`, `camera-pan` → `applyRecipe` · section `recipes`
  Studio: the recipe's controls and its range. Gives up: `camera-shake` is the only procedural jitter of motion; a segment schedule's humanize and the seeds of Shaders and brushes are the other variation.

## Sound

**Music, a voiceover, sound effects**
- Audio clips on the film's timeline, each a music, voiceover or sfx clip with trim, gain, fades and loop, optionally locked to a Scene; the mix ducks music under voiceover → `addAsset`, `addAudioClip`, `updateAudioClip`, `removeAudioClip`, `updateAudioMix` · tool `createMediaUpload`
  Studio: clips as lanes under the timeline; the clip inspector: role, start, duration, volume, fades, loop, lock to a Scene, ducking. Gives up: a clip cannot run past its media unless it loops. Export keeps the loudness; normalizing to −14 LUFS is a switch in Studio's Export.

**A video's own sound**
- Mute, gain and fades on the video object → `setVideoAudio`

## Ready-made starts

**Start from a ready-made move and adjust it**
- A preset expands into ordinary editable Actions: `hard-replace`, `scale-pop`, `blur-slide`, `set-depth`, the text cascades, `odometer`, and the drawn strokes → `applyPreset` · section `presets`
  Gives up: use one only when its expanded Actions are what the moment needs.

## Changing what exists

**Earlier, later, longer, shorter**
- Retime an Action and keep the shape of its keys → `retimeMotionAction`, `updateMotionBlockTiming`
  Studio: drag the Action on the timeline; drag its edges to stretch.
- Move an expression block's range, or a whole group → `updateMotionBlockRange`, `retimeMotionBlockGroup`

**Change one key, add or remove keys**
- Edit keys by id; batch several on one Action → `insertMotionKey`, `updateMotionKey`, `removeMotionKey`, `updateMotionKeyBatch` · `listCapabilities` with no arguments: key `authoringGuide`
  Studio: key markers on the timeline; key values in the inspector. Gives up: prefer these to swapping a whole primitive.

**Give an existing Action another property**
- Add a facet to an Action that already exists: `materializeActionFacets` with the action mode `reuse` → `materializeActionFacets` · tool `getSceneAuthoringContext`
  Gives up: it needs the Action's `expectedActionFingerprint`, which `getSceneAuthoringContext` serves for each Action; read it again after any accept. Giving an Action every facet when it is created needs no fingerprint.

**The design value changed under an animated property**
- Rebase the track onto the new value without moving its keys → `rebasePropertyTrack` · tool `getSceneAuthoringContext`

**Which of two overlapping Actions wins**
- Reorder the Scene's Actions: where replacing Actions overlap, the later one in that order wins → `reorderMotionBlock`
  Studio: drag Action rows within the object's lane.

**Rename, re-stage or remove an Action**
- Name, stage, catalog role, removal → `updateMotionBlockName`, `updateMotionBlockStage`, `updateMotionBlockRole`, `removeMotionBlock`

**Retune Follow Path, Draw or 3D Rotate settings**
- Replace the Action's settings in one edit → `updateFollowPathActionSettings`, `updateDrawEraseActionSettings`, `update3dRotateActionConstants`

## Working with a project and seeing the result

**Find, open or start a project**
- List projects, read one, create one, open it in Studio for a person → tools `listProjects`, `getProject`, `createProject`, `openEditor`

**Make a change and keep it**
- Read each kind's exact input with `listCapabilities` and `kinds`, stage the operations, inspect the candidate, then accept or discard it → sections `operations`, `examples` · `listCapabilities` with no arguments: key `externalAuthoring` · tools `applyOperations`, `acceptOperations`, `discardOperations`
  Gives up: a stage lives 30 minutes, or until what its `scope` covers (one Scene or the project) changes or a newer stage of the same scope replaces it.
- A large batch your own code wrote, such as a whole Scene or many keys, sent as a file so its bytes never pass through the conversation: upload it, then pass the answer's ref as `operationsRef` in place of `operations` → tool `createOperationsUpload` · plugin command `motionade send`
  Gives up: the same checks and batch budgets as inline operations, so a film still goes in several stages; an upload is kept for an hour. Small edits stay inline.

**Share one film among several agents: who works on each Scene, and where it stands**
- Set a Scene's owner and its status (draft, done, reviewed); getProject, and the stage and accept answers, show each note, and flag a reviewed Scene that an accept changed afterwards → tool `setSceneNote`
  Gives up: the note reports and never locks: any agent can still change any Scene. Stages scoped to one Scene are what keep authors of different Scenes from overwriting each other.

**See a moment, see the motion, measure it**
- One frame as a picture; a strip of frames as onion skin or a contact sheet; exact boxes at chosen frames; the pacing of holds and motion → tools `renderFrame`, `renderMotionStrip`, `previewRange`, `getPacingReport`
  Gives up: frames show composition and paths, not rhythm: judge timing at normal speed in Studio.
- Many frames for a script of your own to compare or assemble, fetched as files so the images never pass through the conversation: set `deliver` to link and run the answer's save command → tools `renderFrame`, `renderMotionStrip` · plugin commands `motionade fetch`, `motionade compare`
  Gives up: you do not see the picture yourself, so look at a frame inline when judging it; a link lasts 15 minutes and its file an hour.

**Deliver the film, or export a draft with its sound to check**
- An MP4 of the film or of one Scene, rendered on this machine through Studio's own export: a draft to review, or the file to deliver → tool `createExportLink`
  Studio: Export makes the same file, with a choice of size, quality, frame rate and loudness. Gives up: it needs Chrome or Edge on this machine, and the link reads one revision for 30 minutes: after a change, ask again.

## How to choose

A capability's existence is never a reason to use it; the moment decides. Exact contracts stay in `listCapabilities` and the protocol stays in [Native authoring](authoring.md).

- **Prefer what the designer can adjust.** Catalog Actions created with `materializeActionFacets` are fully editable in Studio. Studio also edits Scale key values on text segments and Repeater targets. Some other routes arrive locked or partly adjustable; the index above names them. When two constructions deliver the moment, choose the one whose handles match the edit the brief predicts.
- **Put shared decisions in one place.** Shared timing in a stagger group or timing style; shared travel on an owner Frame; shared depth in the camera. One edit then retunes the whole relationship.
- **Author each Action whole.** Give an Action every facet it needs at creation; adding one later (`materializeActionFacets` in `reuse` mode) needs the Action's `expectedActionFingerprint`, which `getSceneAuthoringContext` serves in `cas.actionFacets`. To change copy later, use `replaceTextSnapshot` with the snapshot fingerprint `getSceneAuthoringContext` serves in `cas.textSnapshots`; it keeps the Text's motion.
- **Set a style key only where it paints.** `listCapabilities` section `objectProperties` lists each key's kinds in `appliesTo`. Set on any other kind, the key paints nothing, and the stage warns `property_not_applicable`.
- **Approximate honestly.** When the brief asks for something the engine lacks, build the nearest honest construction and say what differs. The index marks what the medium does not have, and [How Motionade works](medium.md) maps After Effects words to what exists here.
